all_dimensional_p_minus_one: For even finite nonzero measures spanning R^n, n>=2, every line-mass ratio strictly below 1/(1+d_n), d_n=2 Gamma(n/2)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma((n-1)/2)), is sufficient. Sharpness for n>=3 is not proved.
feng_hu_li_lv_status: DOI 10.1007/s00208-026-03420-w: official abstract inspected; full text unavailable and uninspected; overlap unverified.
historical_labels: Frozen author audit-pending and unauthenticated-planar-lead statements are historical and preserved. The later audit and SOURCE_UPDATE supersede them only within their stated scope.
nonstrict_constant: For a guarantee stated as line-mass ratio <= c, pi/(pi+2) is a supremum, not an attained largest admissible constant.
numerical_evidence_scope: Finite high-precision regression controls only, not an interval proof or formal certification of continuous theorems.
planar_p_minus_one: Even finite nonzero measures with every antipodal-pair mass ratio strictly below pi/(pi+2) have an origin-symmetric solution. The orthogonal four-atom equality measure has no solution, even among nonsymmetric bodies.
remaining_gap: The general optimal concentration guarantee for p<-1 and higher-dimensional p=-1 sharpness remain unresolved in this work.
